key_insight: Epitaxial α-MnTe thin films on InP(111) show transport signatures consistent with a finite net magnetic polarization, despite bulk MnTe being a compensated antiferromagnet.
engineering_relevance: The work points to a thin-film route for tuning magnetic response in spintronic materials through epitaxial growth, interfaces, and defect engineering.
method: Molecular beam epitaxy growth of α-MnTe on InP(111)
Low-temperature magnetotransport measurements (longitudinal and transverse magnetoresistance)
DFT calculations of bulk and thin-film/defect-induced magnetic behavior
evidence_signal: A hysteretic butterfly-like longitudinal magnetoresistance and nonlinear transverse magnetoresistance were observed, and DFT indicated symmetry breaking or point defects can generate finite magnetization in thin films.
watch_item: Transport signatures imply magnetic polarization but do not by themselves prove the exact microscopic source, so interface and defect effects need direct structural/magnetic verification.
paper_title: Transport Evidence of Magnetic Polarization in the Altermagnetic Candidate MnTe
